target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(codex): dedupe replayed side-question tool calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can replay the same pending `item/tool/call` request when a client connection is rebound. The main attempt path already reuses an in-flight execution by `threadId`, `turnId`, and `callId`, but the `/btw` side-question path did not. A replay there could execute a non-idempotent OpenClaw tool twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing Codex dynamic-tool execution registry in the side-question path.
- Treat `callId` as the protocol request identity: the same `threadId` / `turnId` / `callId` replay shares one execution promise.
- Keep requests with different `callId` values independent, even when their tool names and arguments match.
- Remove the earlier payload-equivalence coalescer, which could suppress a legitimate distinct tool call and misattribute its timeout, diagnostics, or observer callbacks.
- Extend the existing side-question bridge regression test to cover both same-ID replay and distinct-ID execution.

## User Impact

A replayed side-question tool request no longer repeats its external side effect, while intentional calls with distinct Codex call IDs continue to run independently.

## Evidence

- Final PR surface against current `main`: 2 files, +50/-15.
- Upstream Codex contract checked at `openai/codex@0fb559f0f6e2`:
  - `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` defines `call_id` on `DynamicToolCallParams`.
  - `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs` registers pending dynamic-tool responses by `call_id`.
  - `codex-rs/app-server/src/outgoing_message.rs` replays the original pending request when rebinding a connection.
- Regression behavior: two concurrent requests with the same `callId` plus one request with a different `callId` produce three successful protocol responses and exactly two underlying tool executions (`tool-1`, `tool-2`).
- Focused three-file Vitest run: 96/96 passed.
- Final side-question Vitest run: 56/56 passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.88).
- What was not tested: no live Codex connection-rebind E2E was run. Full local tsgo was not usable because the shared dependency tree was stale after merging current `main`; the observed errors were in unrelated packages and no touched Codex file produced an error. The new-head PR CI is the canonical broad proof.

Validation commands:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`
- `git diff --check upstream/main`

target.title: feat(openrouter): forward OpenClaw session id as session_id
target.body:
Optionally forward a stable, OpenRouter-scoped session identifier to OpenRouter as the chat-completion session_id body field. OpenRouter uses it as a sticky routing key (better prompt-cache hits) and for observability. Opt-in per the OpenRouter plugin config (forwardSessionId), off by default; the forwarded value is a SHA-256 hash derived from the active OpenClaw session id (not the raw internal identifier), fits well within OpenRouter's 256-char cap, and never overrides a caller-set value. **Update:** Following ClawSweeper's review, this now forwards an opaque derived identifier instead of the raw OpenClaw session id, per its P1 recommendation ("Derive an OpenRouter-scoped value before merge"). See the "Updated proof" note in the Real behavior proof section below. ## Summary What problem does this PR solve? * OpenRouter accepts a `session_id` to route requests to the same upstream provider, which maximizes prompt-cache hits and improves observability[cite: 1]. * OpenClaw already generates a stable per-session ID, but it was not being forwarded to OpenRouter[cite: 1]. Why does this matter now? * Forwarding the session ID allows OpenRouter to keep a multi-turn OpenClaw session on one upstream provider[cite: 1]. * This improves cache economics and traceability for users[cite: 1]. What is the intended outcome? * Optionally forward a stable, OpenRouter-scoped identifier derived from the active OpenClaw session ID to OpenRouter as the `session_id` request-body field on chat-completion calls[cite: 1]. * This feature is opt-in, configured per model provider (OpenRouter) via the OpenRouter plugin config, and is off by default[cite: 1]. * The derived value is a fixed 64-character SHA-256 hex digest, well under OpenRouter's 256-character limit[cite: 1]. * If a caller-set value already exists, it is never overridden[cite: 1]. What is intentionally out of scope? * Image, music, video, media-understanding, or speech OpenRouter providers (this is for chat/text inference only)[cite: 1]. * Generic provider session forwarding (this is an OpenRouter-specific field)[cite: 1]. * Changing core SDK context types or the shared transport turn-state hook[cite: 1]. * Sending the `x-session-id` header (the body field is sufficient and takes precedence)[cite: 1]. What does success look like? * When enabled, the `session_id` is injected into the OpenRouter chat-completion body[cite: 1]. * When disabled, there is no change to existing behavior (byte-identical payloads)[cite: 1]. What should reviewers focus on? * The implementation in `extensions/openrouter/stream.ts`, specifically the payload-patch wrapper[cite: 1]. * The addition of the boolean flag in the OpenRouter plugin's `configSchema` (`extensions/openrouter/openclaw.plugin.json`)[cite: 1]. * The edge case handling (flag off, caller-set value, over-long ID)[cite: 1].
Summary guidance This PR description is the contributor's durable explanation of the change. Write it for human maintainers first; ClawSweeper and Barnacle use the same text to understand intent, proof, risk, and current review state. Describe the intent and outcome in 2-5 bullets. Avoid restating the diff; reviewers and bots can read the changed files. If this PR fixes a plugin beta-release blocker, title it `fix(): beta blocker - ` and link the matching `Beta blocker: - ` issue labeled `beta-blocker`. Contributors cannot label PRs, so the title is the PR-side signal for maintainers and automation.
## Linked context Which issue does this close? Closes # Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? Related # Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?
Linked context guidance Link the issue, PR, discussion, maintainer request, or owner request that explains why this PR should exist. Maintainer context helps reviewers and automation distinguish intended work from drive-by churn.
## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Forwarding OpenClaw session id to OpenRouter as `session_id`. - Real environment tested: Local macOS environment. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: Enabled `forwardSessionId` and the debug proxy in OpenClaw, then sent a chat request. - Evidence after fix: 1. Intercepted payload captured in data blob `f8acf6e6aa9c226d0a30bdf5`. 2. Extracted `session_id` (`cc8e2503-a840-4fbe-814f-58ff91702d84`) from the proxy blob. 3. OpenRouter dashboard confirming the matching Session ID. 4. The captured terminal output shows the payload sent to OpenRouter correctly includes the generated `session_id` alongside the model and messages. ```text $ git rev-parse --short HEAD && git branch --show-current 913750c2c6 feature/session-forwarding-openrouter $ zcat config/debug-proxy/blobs/f8acf6e6aa9c226d0a30bdf5.bin.gz | grep "{" | jq '.' { "model": "xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw..." } ], "tool_choice": "auto", "max_completion_tokens": 32000, "session_id": "cc8e2503-a840-4fbe-814f-58ff91702d84" } ``` - Observed result after fix: The session ID was correctly injected into the payload and successfully recognized by OpenRouter. - What was not tested: Non-OpenRouter providers. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: None. **Updated proof (opaque derivation revision):** ClawSweeper's review flagged forwarding the *raw* OpenClaw session id as an unapproved identifier-egress contract (P1) and recommended deriving a stable, OpenRouter-specific opaque value instead. This revision replaces the raw pass-through with `deriveOpenRouterSessionId()`, a SHA-256 hash of a namespaced (`openrouter-session:`) form of the session id, so the wrapper never places the raw internal identifier on the wire. - Behavior or issue addressed: Same wrapper/opt-in/route-scoping/non-override plumbing as the original proof above (unchanged); only the *value* written to `session_id` changed, from the raw id to a derived opaque hash. - Real environment tested: Local proof for this revision is a deterministic Node computation plus the full extension test suite; this sandboxed follow-up pass does not have live OpenRouter credentials to re-capture a network payload. The mechanics of the wrapper reaching OpenRouter (opt-in gate, route verification, header/auth handling) are unchanged from the original live-tested revision above. - Exact steps run after this patch: 1. `node -e` computing the derivation directly (reproducible by anyone, no API key needed): ```text $ node -e ' const { createHash } = require("node:crypto"); const raw = "cc8e2503-a840-4fbe-814f-58ff91702d84"; // same id used in the original live capture above console.log(createHash("sha256").update(`openrouter-session:${raw}`).digest("hex")); ' 71b8d97e268e6ed329dc3af63df85c726e58989fa3169781d5b0a2ca268ee5b2 ``` 2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openrouter` — full extension suite, including new tests asserting the derived `session_id` is a 64-char hex digest, differs from the raw id, is deterministic for the same session id, differs across session ids, and stays within the 256-char cap for pathological (5000-char) raw ids. 3. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs`, `pnpm format:check`, and both `knip` deadcode configs (`config/knip.config.ts`, `config/knip.all-exports.config.ts`) — all clean on the changed files. - Evidence after fix: 138/138 tests pass (13 files), including 2 new tests over the prior 137; the payload's `session_id` for the sample raw id above is always `71b8d97e...ee5b2`, never the raw UUID. - Observed result after fix: Same request-shape guarantees as the original proof (opt-in gate, caller-value preservation, non-OpenRouter routes untouched, byte-identical payload when disabled), plus the injected `session_id` is now an opaque derived value rather than the raw session id. - What was not tested: A fresh live OpenRouter network capture of the derived value (blocked by lack of credentials in this pass); the original capture above already established OpenRouter accepts an arbitrary opaque `session_id` string of this shape. - Proof limitations: No live re-capture against OpenRouter's API in this revision; deterministic unit-level proof plus the unchanged (already live-verified) wrapper plumbing stand in for it. **Screenshot of the behaviour on OpenRouter:** **After-fix screenshot:** ## Tests and validation Which commands did you run? * `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openrouter` (138/138 passing)[cite: 1] * `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs`, `pnpm format:check` * `knip` against both `config/knip.config.ts` and `config/knip.all-exports.config.ts` (clean; a prior revision's exported test-only helper was made private after Knip flagged it as unused) What regression coverage was added or updated? * Unit tests in the extension for flag on/off, caller-set payload, and the 256-char cap[cite: 1]. * Negative testing to ensure non-OpenRouter routes do not get `session_id`[cite: 1]. * New: the derived `session_id` is a 64-char hex digest distinct from the raw session id, is deterministic for the same session id across calls, and differs across different session ids. What failed before this fix, if known? * N/A (Additive feature) If no test was added, why not? * N/A
Testing guidance List focused commands, not every incidental check. CI is useful support, but external PRs still need real behavior proof above when behavior changes.
## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) * No (Opt-in feature, default off)[cite: 1] Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) * Yes (New opt-in flag added to OpenRouter plugin configSchema)[cite: 1] Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) * No What is the highest-risk area? * The payload-patch wrapper in `extensions/openrouter/stream.ts`[cite: 1]. How is that risk mitigated? * The feature is additive and default-off[cite: 1]. Existing payloads remain unchanged when disabled[cite: 1]. * The wrapper never overrides a caller-set value, and the forwarded value is a derived opaque SHA-256 hash rather than the raw OpenClaw session id, so enabling the feature does not disclose OpenClaw's internal session identifier to OpenRouter[cite: 1].
Risk guidance Use this for author judgment that is not obvious from the diff. ClawSweeper can see touched files, but it cannot know which behavior you think is risky, why the risk is acceptable, or what mitigation reviewers should verify.
## Current review state What is the next action? * Awaiting maintainer review[cite: 1]. target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: default Docker builds pruned optional bundled plugin runtime dependencies unless operators knew to set `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS`.
- Why it matters: Discord, Feishu, and Voice Call are externalized plugin packages but should be ready in the standard Docker image path.
- What changed: default Docker image builds now include bundled plugin ids `discord`, `feishu`, and `voice-call`; `scripts/docker/setup.sh` uses the same default.
- What did NOT change: operators can still pass `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS=` to build a slimmer image without optional bundled plugin deps.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core already has the correct weighting formula in `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
(`estimateStringChars`). Ollama's extension cannot import core internals, and
exposing that helper through the public plugin SDK would create a new stable
API commitment for a single consumer. This change mirrors the core weighting
locally in `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts` and applies it on the
production stream fallback path only.

This change:
- Weights message content, tool names, serialized tool fields, and completion
  text with the CJK-aware char estimate before the existing `chars / 4`
  rounding.
- Leaves provider-reported `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` authoritative
  when present.
- Proves both (1) the production caller path over real loopback HTTP and
  (2) live generation against a real Ollama daemon, including a strip-proxy
  run that forces the missing-count fallback.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid eval counts, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → guarded fetch → NDJSON parse →
  fallback estimators → `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback
- No public plugin-SDK export added

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama NDJSON stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path writes CJK-aware fallback usage onto
`done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old raw
UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `/api/chat` NDJSON final chunk
without eval counts → `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` /
`estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` → `buildAssistantMessage` →
`done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local `estimateStringChars` mirrors `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts` so the extension
stays inside the plugin boundary without growing the public SDK surface.
Provider-reported eval counts remain authoritative via `resolveUsageCount`.

### Real environment tested

- **Real Ollama daemon**: `ollama` 0.9.6 on macOS arm64, model `qwen2.5:0.5b`,
  listening on `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, Node v22.23.1
- **Case A (provider wins)**: production `createOllamaStreamFn` against the
  real daemon through a same-request pass-through recording proxy.
  `done.message.usage` matched the daemon final-chunk
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` exactly.
- **Case B (CJK fallback)**: same production path through a transparent
  strip-proxy in front of the real daemon. The proxy deletes
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` only on the final NDJSON chunk after the
  daemon has already generated the CJK completion — forcing the production
  fallback. Observed usage matched `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and was
  ~3.8× the naive `length/4` undercount.
- **Harness**: loopback `node:http` Ollama-shaped NDJSON + focused stream
  unit tests (real `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, no fetch mock).

Healthy Ollama almost always emits eval counts, so Case B uses a strip-proxy
in front of the real daemon rather than a fake generator. Generation still
comes from the real model; only the final-chunk usage fields are removed to
enter the production fallback path that this PR fixes.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real daemon (Case A + Case B)
ollama serve
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
# Drive createOllamaStreamFn against :11434 (pass-through + strip-proxy)
# — local proof driver used for the logs below

# Focused harness
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — real daemon, provider counts authoritative (same HTTP response)**

```text
upstream: http://127.0.0.1:11434
model: qwen2.5:0.5b
prompt: 用一句话介绍你自己。请只用中文回答。
node: v22.23.1
ollama: 0.9.6

daemon final-chunk counts (same HTTP response):
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 17, stripped: false }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 40, output: 17, totalTokens: 57, ... }

completion preview: 我是来自阿里云的大规模语言模型，我叫通义千问。
PASS Case A: usage matches same-response prompt_eval_count/eval_count
```

**Case B — real daemon + strip-proxy, CJK-aware fallback**

```text
daemon had counts before strip:
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 33, stripped: true }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 19, output: 60, totalTokens: 79, ... }

completion preview: 我是Qwen，由阿里云自主研发的超大规模语言模型，具有理解、生成文本的能力，并且在人工智能领域有着丰富的经验和深厚的技术积累。

comparison:
  naiveIn: 5          # old length/4 on prompt + "[]"
  naiveOut: 16        # old length/4 on completion
  expectedIn: 19      # estimateStringChars(prompt+"[]")/4
  expectedOut: 60     # estimateStringChars(completion)/4
  observed: { input: 19, output: 60 }
  inflationVsNaiveIn: 3.80x
  inflationVsNaiveOut: 3.75x

PASS Case B: CJK-aware fallback matches estimateStringChars/4 (>> naive length/4)
```

**Focused harness (production path, loopback NDJSON)**

```text
 ✓ stream.test.ts > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback
 ✓ stream.test.ts > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > estimates CJK-aware usage when a real Ollama-shaped stream omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the HTTP fallback
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real Ollama 0.9.6 daemon (`qwen2.5:0.5b`):

1. When eval counts are present, `done.message.usage` equals those daemon
   counts (`input: 40`, `output: 17` on the recorded Case A request).
2. When final-chunk eval counts are stripped after real CJK generation,
   fallback usage is CJK-aware (`input: 19`, `output: 60`) — about 3.8× the
   old naive `length/4` undercount, and identical to
   `estimateStringChars(...)/4`.

### What was not tested

- Full gateway `/context` treemap UI and end-to-end `shouldCompact` compaction
  trigger against a long CJK session
- Ollama Cloud / remote multi-host endpoints
- Non-qwen model families (fallback math is model-agnostic; only the missing
  eval-count trigger matters)

### Fix classification

bugfix — usage accounting / CJK undercount

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the local CJK mirror (no public SDK export),
real-daemon Case A/B proof, loopback HTTP caller-path proof, and CI
unused-export cleanup.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- merge-risk: auth-provider — both fixes add defensive guards without changing auth flow or error semantics. The Vertex ADC fix wraps an existing error path in a clearer message; the QA Lab fix adds body cleanup before existing throws. No credential path, token exchange, or provider selection logic is altered.

target.title: fix(gmail): prevent duplicate watch renewals during stalls
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. ## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities

- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
